question: Cataract is the single leading cause of avoidable (preventable and treatable) blindness in India, accounting for approximately 66% of all blind persons, and remains the primary target of the National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Cataract is the leading cause of avoidable blindness in India (~66%). The NPCBVI targets cataract surgical rate (CSR: surgeries per million population per year) as its principal indicator. Refractive error is the second leading cause globally but cataract leads in India in absolute blind persons.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — TRUE. Cataract accounts for approximately 66% of blindness in India (NPCBVI 2015–19 data). It is avoidable by surgical correction (ECCE/phacoemulsification + IOL). Vision 2020 and NPCBVI both prioritise cataract surgical rate (CSR) as a key performance metric for India.
